revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Making Moves
revealWordProblem.text: A group of friends are planning to make a movie. They research the running times of movies made. The data they collected are shown in the histogram. They have asked for your advice on how long their movie should run. What do you recommend? Explain your recommendation based on the data presented in the histogram.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Add up the histogram's frequencies: 7 + 30 + 39 + 22 + 12 + 2 + 1 + 1 = 114 movies total. The tallest bar is the 101–115 minute interval with 39 movies, the mode of the data. Combined with the neighboring 86–100 minute interval (30 movies), that's 30 + 39 = 69 of the 114 movies, or 69 ÷ 114 ≈ 0.605 = 60.5%, running between 86 and 115 minutes. Very few movies run longer than 145 minutes (2 + 1 + 1 = 4 movies, about 3.5%). Based on this data, I'd recommend the friends aim for a running time in the 101–115 minute range, since that's the most common length and keeps their movie in line with most movies made.

conceptIntro.heading: Let's build it together — What is a histogram?
conceptIntro.intro: A histogram is a bar graph that groups numbers into equal ranges called intervals. The height of each bar is the frequency: how many values fall in that interval. The bars touch because the intervals are continuous. We'll walk through a worked example, try one together, then you'll try a few with hints right there when you need them.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: Each bar's height shows how many data values land inside that interval.

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: My data: 3, 7, 12, 15, 18, 24. I will use intervals of 10: 0–9, 10–19, 20–29.
Interval 0–9: the values 3 and 7 fit, so the frequency is 2.
Interval 10–19: the values 12, 15, and 18 fit, so the frequency is 3.
Interval 20–29: only the value 24 fits, so the frequency is 1.
Now I draw three bars with heights 2, 3, and 1, touching each other. The tallest bar (10–19) is where most values are.

weDo.title: Let's try together
lines: New data: 2, 4, 8, 11, 13, 16, 21. We will use intervals of 10 again: 0–9, 10–19, 20–29.
How many values fall in 0–9? Count them. How many fall in 10–19?
How many fall in 20–29? Which interval would have the tallest bar?
Sentence frame — say it with me: "The multiples/steps I need are ___ , and the answer is ___ ."

approaching.stem: A histogram shows these frequencies: 0–4: 3 players, 5–9: 8 players, 10–14: 12 players, 15–19: 5 players. How many players are represented in total?
choiceFeedback: That total leaves out part of the data. Every bar contributes, so add all four frequencies together — including the shortest bar.
Did you count frequencies or find the highest value?
Add all frequencies: 3+8+12+5.
hints: The question asks for the TOTAL across all four intervals — not the tallest bar and not the biggest interval.
Each frequency counts the players in one interval, and no player is counted twice — so combine all four frequencies into one total.
Set up the addition: 3 + 8 + 12 + 5. The sum of all the bar heights is the total number of players.
approaching.stemEs: Un histograma muestra estas frecuencias: 0–4: 3 jugadores, 5–9: 8 jugadores, 10–14: 12 jugadores, 15–19: 5 jugadores. ¿Cuántos jugadores se representan en total?
hintsEs: La pregunta pide el TOTAL de los cuatro intervalos, no la barra más alta ni el intervalo más grande.
Cada frecuencia cuenta los jugadores de un intervalo, y ningún jugador se cuenta dos veces, así que combina las cuatro frecuencias en un solo total.
Plantea la suma: 3 + 8 + 12 + 5. La suma de todas las alturas de las barras es el total de jugadores.

approaching.stem: In a histogram, what does the height of each bar represent?
choices: The average of the data in that interval
The frequency (count) of data in that interval
approaching.explanation: Each bar's height shows the frequency — how many data values fall within that interval.
choiceFeedback: A bar height is not something you calculate from the values — it is something you tally. Think about what you would count to make the bar taller.
Height shows how many—does it show the typical value?
Range is the interval spread, not the height.
hints: Think about what you'd count to draw one bar: you'd tally how many data values land inside that interval.
Height is a COUNT, not a calculation — no averaging, no middle values. Ask which choice simply says 'how many.'
First step: imagine the interval 10–14 holding the values 11, 12, 12, 14. Its bar would rise to 4 — because 4 values fall inside.
approaching.stemEs: En un histograma, ¿qué representa la altura de cada barra?
approaching.explanationEs: La altura de cada barra muestra la frecuencia: cuántos valores de datos caen dentro de ese intervalo.
choicesEs: El promedio de los datos de ese intervalo
La frecuencia (el conteo) de datos en ese intervalo
hintsEs: Piensa qué contarías para dibujar una barra: contarías cuántos datos caen dentro de ese intervalo.
La altura es un CONTEO, no un cálculo: sin promedios ni valores del medio. Pregunta qué opción simplemente dice 'cuántos'.
Primer paso: imagina el intervalo 10–14 con los valores 11, 12, 12, 14. Su barra llegaría a 4, porque 4 valores caen adentro.

approaching.stem: How is a histogram different from a regular bar graph?
choices: Histogram bars touch (no gaps) because the intervals are continuous ranges
Histograms use colors and bar graphs don't
Bar graphs show numbers and histograms show words
approaching.explanation: In a histogram, bars touch because each interval connects to the next (0–9, 10–19, etc.) — the data is continuous.
choiceFeedback: There is a real structural difference between the two graphs. Look at the spacing between the bars and at what the horizontal axis is measuring.
Histograms always show intervals—this is the key difference.
Colors don't define a histogram—structure does.
hints: Picture both graphs side by side: one has spaces between its bars, one doesn't. Ask why that would be.
Think about the x-axis: categories like 'red, blue, green' can be separated, but number intervals like 0–9 and 10–19 connect end to end.
First step: write two neighboring intervals, 0–9 and 10–19. Notice that 10 starts right where 9 ends — that's why the bars behave differently.
approaching.stemEs: ¿En qué se diferencia un histograma de una gráfica de barras común?
approaching.explanationEs: En un histograma las barras se tocan porque cada intervalo se conecta con el siguiente (0–9, 10–19, etc.): los datos son continuos.
choicesEs: Las barras del histograma se tocan (sin espacios) porque los intervalos son rangos continuos
Los histogramas usan colores y las gráficas de barras no
Las gráficas de barras muestran números y los histogramas muestran palabras
hintsEs: Imagina las dos gráficas lado a lado: una tiene espacios entre las barras y la otra no. Pregunta por qué sería así.
Piensa en el eje x: categorías como 'rojo, azul, verde' se pueden separar, pero intervalos numéricos como 0–9 y 10–19 se conectan de punta a punta.
Primer paso: escribe dos intervalos vecinos, 0–9 y 10–19. Nota que el 10 empieza justo donde termina el 9: por eso las barras se comportan distinto.

approaching.stem: A histogram has intervals: 0–4, 5–9, 10–14, 15–19. What is the width of each interval?
approaching.explanation: Each interval covers 5 values (0,1,2,3,4 then 5,6,7,8,9 etc.), so the width is 5.
choiceFeedback: That span covers two intervals joined together. Count the values inside a single interval, from its first number through its last.
Start is 0, end is 4—that's width 4, not 10.
The width is the span of each interval: 4−0=4 or 5−0=5.
hints: Width means how many whole-number values fit inside one interval — count them, don't just subtract the endpoints.
List the values in the first interval, 0–4: count every whole number from 0 up to and including 4.
Count aloud: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 — how many numbers did you say? Check that the interval 5–9 holds the same amount.
approaching.stemEs: Un histograma tiene los intervalos: 0–4, 5–9, 10–14, 15–19. ¿Cuál es el ancho de cada intervalo?
approaching.explanationEs: Cada intervalo cubre 5 valores (0, 1, 2, 3, 4 y luego 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, etc.), así que el ancho es 5.
hintsEs: El ancho significa cuántos valores enteros caben dentro de un intervalo — cuéntalos, no solo restes los extremos.
Enumera los valores del primer intervalo, 0–4: cuenta cada número entero desde 0 hasta 4 inclusive.
Cuenta en voz alta: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 — ¿cuántos números dijiste? Revisa que el intervalo 5–9 tenga la misma cantidad.

approaching.stem: A histogram bar for the interval 20–29 reaches a height of 7. What does the 7 tell you?
approaching.explanation: A bar's height is the frequency — here, 7 values land in the 20–29 interval.
choiceFeedback: The height is not one of the data values itself. It records how many pieces of data landed inside that interval.
Largest value is somewhere in 20–29, not necessarily 7.
Seven intervals would be many—count the intervals shown.
hints: Two numbers appear here: the interval (20–29) and the height (7). Keep straight which one is a range and which is a count.
A bar's height always answers 'how many data values landed here?' Ask yourself what the 7 is counting.
First step: say it as a sentence — 'the bar for 20–29 rises to 7.' Now finish the sentence: '7 what?' Pick the choice that completes it.
approaching.stemEs: En un histograma, la barra del intervalo 20–29 llega a una altura de 7. ¿Qué te dice el 7?
approaching.explanationEs: La altura de una barra es la frecuencia: aquí, 7 valores caen en el intervalo 20–29.
choicesEs: 7 valores de datos caen entre 20 y 29
hintsEs: Aquí aparecen dos números: el intervalo (20–29) y la altura (7). Ten claro cuál es un rango y cuál es un conteo.
La altura de una barra siempre responde '¿cuántos datos cayeron aquí?' Pregúntate qué está contando el 7.
Primer paso: dilo como oración: 'la barra de 20–29 llega a 7'. Ahora completa la oración: '¿7 qué?' Elige la opción que la complete.

approaching.title: Spot the Counting Mistake

workedExample.label: Conclusion
workedExample.work: So the histogram bars have heights 2, 2, and 1.
workedExample.workEs: Así que las barras del histograma tienen alturas 2, 2 y 1.

approaching.correctWork: The student missed a value in the 10–19 interval. The values 11, 13, AND 16 all fall in 10–19, so its frequency is 3, not 2. The correct frequency counts are 0–9: 2 (the 3 and 7), 10–19: 3 (the 11, 13, and 16), and 20–29: 1 (the 22), which totals 6 — the same as the 6 data values.
hints: Count the data values first: 3, 7, 11, 13, 16, 22 is 6 values, but the frequencies add to only 5. A value was missed.
Check the 10–19 interval carefully — list every value from 10 to 19 in the data set.
approaching.explanation: There are 6 data values but the student's frequencies add to only 5, which is the tip-off. The interval 10–19 holds 11, 13, and 16, so its frequency is 3, making the correct bar heights 2, 3, and 1.
approaching.explanationEs: Hay 6 valores de datos, pero las frecuencias del estudiante suman apenas 5, y esa es la pista. El intervalo 10–19 contiene 11, 13 y 16, así que su frecuencia es 3, y las alturas correctas de las barras son 2, 3 y 1.
approaching.correctWorkEs: Al estudiante se le escapó un valor del intervalo 10–19. Los valores 11, 13 Y 16 caen todos en 10–19, así que su frecuencia es 3, no 2. Los conteos correctos son 0–9: 2 (el 3 y el 7), 10–19: 3 (el 11, el 13 y el 16) y 20–29: 1 (el 22), que suman 6 — igual que los 6 valores de datos.
hintsEs: Cuenta primero los valores: 3, 7, 11, 13, 16, 22 son 6 valores, pero las frecuencias suman solo 5. Se saltó un valor.
Revisa con cuidado el intervalo 10–19 — enumera cada valor del 10 al 19 en el conjunto de datos.

onLevel.stem: A histogram of test scores shows: 50–59: 2, 60–69: 5, 70–79: 10, 80–89: 8, 90–99: 3. Which interval has the most students?
onLevel.explanation: The 70–79 interval has the highest frequency of 10 students.
choiceFeedback: That interval holds the highest scores, but the question asks where the most students are. Compare the frequencies, not the score ranges.
5 is less than 10—which bar is tallest?
Compare: 2, 5, 10, 8, 3—the largest is 10.
hints: 'Most students' means the highest frequency — compare the counts 2, 5, 10, 8, 3, not the score ranges themselves.
Careful: the highest scores (90–99) don't mean the most students. Find the largest of the five frequencies first, then read off its interval.
First step: circle the largest number among 2, 5, 10, 8, 3. Then match that count back to its interval — and check the choice pairs both parts.
onLevel.stemEs: Un histograma de calificaciones muestra: 50–59: 2, 60–69: 5, 70–79: 10, 80–89: 8, 90–99: 3. ¿Qué intervalo tiene la mayor cantidad de estudiantes?
onLevel.explanationEs: El intervalo 70–79 tiene la frecuencia más alta, con 10 estudiantes.
hintsEs: 'La mayoría de los estudiantes' significa la frecuencia más alta — compara los conteos 2, 5, 10, 8, 3, no los rangos de puntajes.
Cuidado: los puntajes más altos (90–99) no significan la mayor cantidad de estudiantes. Halla primero la mayor de las cinco frecuencias y luego lee su intervalo.
Primer paso: encierra el número más grande entre 2, 5, 10, 8, 3. Luego relaciona ese conteo con su intervalo — y revisa que la opción incluya ambas partes.

onLevel.stem: A histogram of goals-per-game shows: 0–1: 9 players, 2–3: 6, 4–5: 3, 6–7: 1. What shape is this distribution?
choices: Skewed right (most players low, tail toward high values)
Skewed left (most players high, tail toward low values)
onLevel.explanation: The tallest bars are at the low end (0–1) and the bars shrink as goals increase — the tail points right, so it is skewed right.
choiceFeedback: A symmetric shape would have the bars mirroring each other around the center. Compare the 9 at the low end with the 1 at the high end.
Are the bars roughly equal height? This isn't symmetric.
Most are low (left), tail goes high (right)—that's right skew.
hints: Sketch the bars: heights 9, 6, 3, 1 from left to right. Notice which side is tall and which way the heights trail off.
Skew is named for the TAIL — the long, low side — not for the peak. Find the direction the bars shrink toward, then name that direction.
First step: the tallest bar (9 players) is at 0–1 goals on the left, and heights fall to 1 by 6–7. Trace the tail with your finger, then name it.
onLevel.stemEs: Un histograma de goles por partido muestra: 0–1: 9 jugadores, 2–3: 6, 4–5: 3, 6–7: 1. ¿Qué forma tiene esta distribución?
onLevel.explanationEs: Las barras más altas están en el extremo bajo (0–1) y se van encogiendo a medida que aumentan los goles: la cola apunta a la derecha, así que está sesgada a la derecha.
choicesEs: Sesgada a la derecha (la mayoría de los jugadores abajo, con cola hacia los valores altos)
Sesgada a la izquierda (la mayoría de los jugadores arriba, con cola hacia los valores bajos)
hintsEs: Dibuja las barras: alturas 9, 6, 3, 1 de izquierda a derecha. Fíjate qué lado es alto y hacia dónde bajan las alturas.
La asimetría se nombra por la COLA —el lado largo y bajo—, no por el pico. Halla la dirección hacia donde se encogen las barras y nómbrala.
Primer paso: la barra más alta (9 jugadores) está en 0–1 goles a la izquierda, y las alturas bajan a 1 en 6–7. Traza la cola con el dedo y nómbrala.

onLevel.title: Spot the Interval Mistake

workedExample.label: Conclusion
workedExample.work: The student drew three bars and said the histogram was complete.
workedExample.workEs: El estudiante dibujó tres barras y dijo que el histograma estaba completo.

onLevel.correctWork: The intervals are not equal in width and they leave a gap. 0–5 and 6–10 each cover 6 values, but 12–18 covers 7 values and the value 11 has no bin at all. Histogram intervals must be equal-width and cover every value with no gaps. Using equal intervals of 5 (0–4, 5–9, 10–14, 15–19) gives frequencies 0–4: 2 (the 1 and 4), 5–9: 2 (the 6 and 9), 10–14: 1 (the 12), and 15–19: 2 (the 15 and 18), totaling 7.
hints: Check the width of each interval the student used. Are 0–5, 6–10, and 12–18 all the same size?
Where would a value of 11 go? Every value needs exactly one equal-width bin — there can be no gaps.
onLevel.explanation: The problem starts at the interval-choosing step: 0–5 and 6–10 are 6 wide, 12–18 is 7 wide, and the value 11 has nowhere to go. Equal-width bins of 5 fix both problems — 0–4: 2, 5–9: 2, 10–14: 1, 15–19: 2, totaling all 7 assist values.
onLevel.explanationEs: El problema empieza en el paso de elegir intervalos: 0–5 y 6–10 miden 6, 12–18 mide 7, y el valor 11 no tiene dónde ir. Casillas del mismo ancho de 5 arreglan las dos cosas: 0–4: 2, 5–9: 2, 10–14: 1, 15–19: 2, lo que cubre los 7 valores de asistencias.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: Los intervalos no tienen el mismo ancho y dejan un hueco. 0–5 y 6–10 cubren 6 valores cada uno, pero 12–18 cubre 7 valores y el valor 11 no tiene intervalo. Los intervalos de un histograma deben tener el mismo ancho y cubrir todos los valores sin huecos. Con intervalos iguales de 5 (0–4, 5–9, 10–14, 15–19) las frecuencias son 0–4: 2 (el 1 y el 4), 5–9: 2 (el 6 y el 9), 10–14: 1 (el 12) y 15–19: 2 (el 15 y el 18), que suman 7.
hintsEs: Revisa el ancho de cada intervalo que usó el estudiante. ¿0–5, 6–10 y 12–18 son todos del mismo tamaño?
¿Dónde iría un valor de 11? Cada valor necesita exactamente un intervalo del mismo ancho — no puede haber huecos.

onLevel.stem: Data: 4, 8, 9, 12, 14, 15, 17, 18, 19, 22, 24, 27, 31, 33. How many values fall in the 10–19 interval?
onLevel.explanation: The values 12, 14, 15, 17, 18, and 19 all fall between 10 and 19, so the frequency for that bin is 6.
choiceFeedback: That count sweeps in values from outside the interval. Only numbers from 10 through 19 belong in this bin.
Did you count correctly which values fall in 10–19?
Not all values fit in that interval—count carefully.
onLevel.stemEs: Datos: 4, 8, 9, 12, 14, 15, 17, 18, 19, 22, 24, 27, 31, 33. ¿Cuántos valores caen en el intervalo 10–19?
onLevel.explanationEs: Los valores 12, 14, 15, 17, 18 y 19 caen entre 10 y 19, así que la frecuencia de ese intervalo es 6.
hints: A frequency is just a count of how many values land inside one interval, endpoints included.
Go through the list in order and mark only the numbers that are at least 10 and no more than 19.
The first value in that range is 12, and 9 is too small to count. Keep working down the list and tally the ones that qualify.
hintsEs: Una frecuencia es simplemente el conteo de cuántos valores caen dentro de un intervalo, incluyendo los extremos.
Recorre la lista en orden y marca solo los números que sean al menos 10 y no más de 19.
El primer valor en ese rango es 12, y el 9 es demasiado pequeño para contar. Sigue bajando por la lista y cuenta los que califican.

onLevel.stem: Frequencies: 0–9: 3, 10–19: 9, 20–29: 5, 30–39: 2. Which interval has the tallest bar?
onLevel.explanation: The 10–19 interval has the greatest frequency (9 players), so its bar is the tallest.
choiceFeedback: That interval sits in the middle of the range, but height depends on the count. Compare the frequencies 3, 9, 5, and 2 directly.
The tallest bar shows the highest frequency—which interval is it?
Compare 3, 9, 5, 2—which number is biggest?
onLevel.stemEs: Frecuencias: 0–9: 3, 10–19: 9, 20–29: 5, 30–39: 2. ¿Qué intervalo tiene la barra más alta?
onLevel.explanationEs: El intervalo 10–19 tiene la mayor frecuencia (9 jugadores), así que su barra es la más alta.
hints: Bar height comes from the frequency, not from how large the numbers in the interval are.
List the four frequencies on their own and compare them as plain numbers.
The counts are 3, 9, 5, and 2. Decide which of those is greatest and read off the interval it belongs to.
hintsEs: La altura de una barra viene de la frecuencia, no de qué tan grandes son los números del intervalo.
Escribe las cuatro frecuencias por separado y compáralas como números simples.
Los conteos son 3, 9, 5 y 2. Decide cuál es el mayor y lee el intervalo al que pertenece.

onLevel.stem: Read this histogram of assists per game — 0–4: 2 players, 5–9: 8 players, 10–14: 5 players, 15–19: 1 player. About how many players are on the team?
onLevel.explanation: Add every bar's frequency: 2 + 8 + 5 + 1 = 16 players total.
choiceFeedback: That sum leaves one of the bars out. Every interval contributes, so add all four frequencies: 2, 8, 5, and 1.
Not quite. Add every bar's frequency: 2 + 8 + 5 + 1 = ___ players total.
Histogram shows frequency by interval, not individual values.
onLevel.stemEs: Lee este histograma de asistencias por partido: 0–4: 2 jugadores, 5–9: 8 jugadores, 10–14: 5 jugadores, 15–19: 1 jugador. ¿Aproximadamente cuántos jugadores hay en el equipo?
onLevel.explanationEs: Suma la frecuencia de cada barra: 2 + 8 + 5 + 1 = 16 jugadores en total.
hints: Every player in the data set is counted in exactly one bar, so no one is left out and no one is doubled.
Find the team size by adding the frequencies of all the bars together.
Start with 2 + 8 = 10, then keep adding the remaining two frequencies.
hintsEs: Cada jugador del conjunto de datos se cuenta en exactamente una barra, así que nadie queda fuera ni se cuenta dos veces.
Halla el tamaño del equipo sumando las frecuencias de todas las barras.
Comienza con 2 + 8 = 10 y luego sigue sumando las otras dos frecuencias.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Display Data: Histograms is counting a boundary value in two intervals at once — for example, putting the value 10 in both the '0–9' bin and the '10–19' bin. Each data value belongs to exactly ONE interval. Before you submit, add up all your frequencies and check that the total matches the number of data values you started with.

optionalActivity.name: Histogram Builder Lab
optionalActivity.intro: Optional — one more together if the group is ready: Sort game-day stats into bins, build the bars, and read what the histogram says about the team.

diagram.title: Shots Per Game — Team Histogram
diagram.caption: The tallest bars sit at 3–5 and 6–8 shots: 18 of the 23 players cluster there.

connect.scenario: A soccer coach looks at a histogram of shots-per-game for the team: 0–2 shots: 1 player, 3–5 shots: 8 players, 6–8 shots: 10 players, 9–11 shots: 3 players, 12–14 shots: 1 player. The coach says, 'Most of my players take a good number of shots.'

histogram.title: Shots Per Game — Team Histogram
histogram.caption: Read the shape: where do most players cluster?

connect.promptQuestion: Does the histogram support the coach's claim? What does the shape of the data tell you?
connect.prompt: The histogram peaks at the ___ interval with ___ players. The shape is approximately ___. This ___ the coach's claim because ___.

check.stem: Which interval has the most players?
check.explanation: The 6–8 interval has 10 players — the tallest bar in the histogram.

check.stem: How many players take between 3 and 8 shots per game?
check.explanation: 8 players in the 3–5 bar plus 10 players in the 6–8 bar = 18 of the 23 players.

check.stem: Does the histogram support the coach's claim?
choices: Yes — 18 of 23 players cluster in the middle intervals
No — the data is skewed right
You cannot tell from a histogram
check.explanation: The distribution is roughly symmetric with a clear center at 6–8 shots, and most players (18 of 23) sit in the two middle bars. That backs up 'most of my players take a good number of shots'.

connect.modelAnswer: The histogram peaks at the 6–8 interval with 10 players, and the shape is roughly symmetric — it rises to a center and falls off on both sides. This supports the coach's claim: 18 of the 23 players sit in the 3–5 and 6–8 intervals, so most players really do take a solid number of shots.

exitTicket.stem: Quick check — you've got this: A histogram of player heights shows: 60–63 in: 2, 64–67 in: 7, 68–71 in: 9, 72–75 in: 4. Which interval has the most players?
exitTicket.explanation: The 68–71 inch interval has the highest frequency of 9 players.
choiceFeedback: That interval has 4 — compare each bar's frequency.
That's the smallest count (2) — look for the tallest bar.
That has 7 — check which interval has the highest frequency.
hints: 'Most players' points to frequency — compare the counts 2, 7, 9, and 4, not which heights have the biggest inches.
Find the largest of the four frequencies first, then trace it back to its height interval. Don't pick the interval with the tallest players.
First step: list the counts in the order given — 2, 7, 9, 4. Circle the biggest one, then match it back to its interval in the stem.

questions.stem: A box plot shows: Min = 10, Q1 = 15, Median = 20, Q3 = 28, Max = 35. What is the interquartile range (IQR)?
What percentage of data falls between Q1 and Q3 on a box plot?
questions.explanation: The box in a box plot contains the middle 50% of the data (from Q1 to Q3).

questions.stem: On a box plot, what does the line inside the box represent?
questions.explanation: The line inside the box of a box plot always represents the median.
